contribution.position: Holding my earlier position. Answering product's claim that reliability is settled because nobody else sees a problem: that is absence of objection, not evidence. artifact:incident-log shows a 30-day error rate of 1.8% against a 0.3% SLO (six times over) and two sev2 incidents, and product's own cited artifact, artifact:cost-sheet, covers only infra spend and says nothing about reliability. It cannot settle this axis. The other roles' evidence is real but answers different questions. qa's artifact:test-report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) shows functional correctness, not production error behavior. ops's artifact:ops-runbook shows that deploy and rollback steps exist, which limits blast radius but does not reduce the error rate. New point since my last turn: the artifact list contains no root-cause analysis of the two sev2s and no pre/post error-rate comparison or canary data, so nothing shows whether the change touches the failing paths. artifact:perf-report (p99 within budget at peak) covers latency, not errors. Until evidence of that kind exists, reliability stays open.
